title: Parity-sharp polyhomogeneous mapping of weighted geodesic X-ray transforms on nontrapping manifolds with strictly convex boundary
source_title: Double b-fibrations and desingularization of the X-ray transform on manifolds with strictly convex boundary
author: Rafe Mazzeo; François Monard
difficulty_reason: A direct use of the ordinary pushforward theorem overestimates the boundary index set and does not recover the selected scattering-even support. The authors build a resolved geodesic double b-fibration and compatible scattering coordinates, then establish the involution symmetry of the coefficient integrals that removes odd powers of the geodesic length. That new geometric and parity core identifies the transformed exponent/log support, beyond merely invoking the allowed polyhomogeneous calculus foundations.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Theorem2.1 first mapping/index assertion only: nontrapping smooth Riemannian manifold with strictly convex boundary, smooth weight onSM, a polyhomogeneous input withC-infinity index setE andinf(E)>-1; output has scattering-even index set contained in{(2z+1,l):(z,l)inE}. Read full geometric desingularization14–18, special coordinates19–21, coordinate invariance21–23 and full weighted-integral expansion24. Named prior first-exit smoothness and boundary factorization22/Prop6.12 plus Melrose conormal pullback/pushforward are identified foundations. No backprojection theorem2.2 or numerical leading coefficient claimed. Exact leading coefficient10 is excluded because source16 statesF onglancing equalsII while its endpointF=mu/tau and source21tau/mu=2/II implyF=II/2; preserve originals and record this internal factor-two discrepancy. Formula22 also prints2^k uniformly inlog degree rather than2^ell, but the selected index assertion uses only the set of logarithmic degrees and explicit binomial expansion, not coefficient values. PDF authors Rafe Mazzeo and Francois Monard,11/2024/266/license verified.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The author desingularizes collapsing glancing geodesics into a double b-fibration, builds coordinates adapted to the scattering involution and uses parity of the rescaled geodesic integrals to obtain sharp doubled boundary exponents. This exceeds qualifying-exam microlocal analysis.
